title: Compact decorator API for resumable streaming chat + resilient retry semantics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: client code that consumes streaming chat completions today must wire together low-level event parsing, checkpoint persistence, idempotency keys, and retry logic. This causes repetition, brittle resume behavior on transient network errors, and inconsistent telemetry across integrations.

Goal: provide a compact, composable decorator-based surface for the Python SDK that: 
- Lets application code declare a single function to receive ordered high-level chat events (tokens, delta messages, function calls, done/err signals).
- Handles durable resume/checkpoint tokens and optional user-provided persistent storage hooks.
- Implements adaptive retry semantics (safe retry on idempotent points, fallback to resumable replay otherwise).
- Exposes backpressure signals and cancellation hooks so frameworks (FastAPI, Celery) can integrate cleanly.
- Emits consistent telemetry spans and failure classifications for platform SLO analysis.

Scope: SDK-side ergonomic API + companion examples; server-side resume token format is out of scope (assumes existing resume token contract).
acceptance_criteria: Provide @stream_handler decorator that converts raw streaming event frames into typed ChatEvent objects and routes to user callback
Decorator supports an optional checkpoint_store hook with read/write signatures and integrates with a resumable token stored per-session

Retries: transient network errors trigger automatic reconnect with exponential backoff up to a configurable attempt budget; if server acknowledges resume token, resume is verified; otherwise, fallback to deterministic replay mode and surface a RecoverableReplayError to the handler
Backpressure API: handler may await StreamControl.pause() and StreamControl.resume() to throttle consumption; default is unthrottled streaming with safe buffer limits
Extensive unit and integration tests covering: normal stream, mid-stream network drop + resume, token corruption, intentional cancel, and large message fanout
Docs: cookbooks showing QuickStart, FastAPI integration, and migration notes from older event iterators
Telemetry: each stream produces a trace with token_id, resume_count, retry_reason, total_tokens and a labeled metric for resumed_vs_fresh streams
design_notes: Checkpoint contract: checkpoint_store.read(session_id)->str|None, checkpoint_store.write(session_id, token:str)->None. Implementations will be given for in-memory, Redis (recommended), and S3-based long-term storage

Retry model: classify errors into transient (network, 5xx) vs terminal (400-range model errors). On transient: attempt reconnect and supply last known resume token. If server refuses resume (mismatch), perform deterministic replay by re-issuing request with the full prompt history and a server-side replay marker
Backpressure: small bounded asyncio.Queue used by default; control.pause() drains upstream reads and applies cooperative yield; signal used in streaming backends to reduce buffer pressure

Security: resume tokens can contain opaque IDs; SDK will not parse token contents and will treat them as opaque strings. Recommend encrypting persisted tokens with customer KMS for private deployments
implementation_plan: Week 1: implement core decorator and ChatEvent data model, add in-memory checkpoint store and basic docs
Week 2: integrate retry/connect logic and server resume exchange flow; build Redis checkpoint plugin and unit tests for resume happy path
Week 3: implement backpressure control object and FastAPI example integration; add telemetry spans and metrics export hooks
Week 4: expand tests to cover token corruption and replay fallback; run interop tests against staging runtime; iterate on API ergonomics from early feedback
Week 5: docs finalization, cookbook PRs, and release in py-sdk-0.6.0 with migration guide
telemetry_and_metrics: Trace tags: session_id, resume_token_present (bool), resume_count (int), retry_reason (string), final_status (ok|error|cancel)
Logs: structured warning when token mismatches lead to replay, include safe redaction of token IDs
Alerting: high ratio of streams_replayed vs streams_resumed indicates runtime resume-contract regressions
compatibility_migration_notes: Older iterators returned raw event dicts; migration path: replace for-loop over iterate_events(...) with @stream_handler-decorated function and use ChatEvent semantics
If customers relied on low-level SSE framing, provide a transitional shim module `legacy_adapter` that adapts old callbacks to new decorator surface
Default behavior preserves existing timeouts but introduces a per-stream retry budget which can be configured globally via SDKClient(stream_retry_budget=...)
docs_and_examples: FastAPI integration: examples/python/fastapi_stream_endpoint.py showing cancellation propagation from request client to stream handler
Cookbook: docs/sdk/streaming/resume_and_retries.md describing failure modes and recommended storage backends
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/3307 -- redis checkpoint plugin and FastAPI example
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: resume token contract changes on server causing mass replays. Mitigation: emit metric streams_replayed and alert on increases; provide emergency opt-out flag to disable resume and fall back to fresh requests
Risk: large persistent stores (S3) introduce latency when writing checkpoints. Mitigation: write asynchronously and keep latest token in local cache; expose write_policy option (sync|async|batched)
Risk: decorator hides too much internal behavior leading to surprising developer debugging UX. Mitigation: debug mode toggles verbose event logs and exposes raw frames via control.debug_stream()
test_plan: Unit tests for ChatEvent parsing, checkpoint read/write semantics, and control.pause/resume
Integration test: simulate mid-stream TCP drop and assert resume path uses persisted token and that handler receives no duplicate events (idempotency verified)
Fuzz test: corrupt persisted token and confirm SDK falls back to replay with clear RecoverableReplayError surfaced to handler
E2E staging run against runtime-staging with synthetic traffic to validate telemetry and latency impact
deployment_and_rollout: Feature branch -> internal canary: enable new decorator by default for internal SDK consumers via environment toggle SDK_STREAM_HANDLER_CANARY=true
Gradual rollout: stage usage in 10% of SDK CI jobs, monitor streams_replayed metric for 72h, then enable globally
Docs: add migration doc and announce in SDK release notes with code samples and FAQ
